# glinet_network_advanced (Resource)

Manages the advanced network settings of the router: Full Cone NAT and the SIP ALG (`network.set_advance_config` in the router API). The router has one configuration of these settings, so use one instance of this resource. Each write sends both values, as the web UI does. An attribute that is not set keeps the value of the router: the provider sends back the value that it reads from the router just before the write. What the router restarts for the write is not known. The write of this resource was not tested on a router; the parameters come from the router's web UI. Destroy removes the resource from the Terraform state and does not change the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "glinet_network_advanced" "this" {
  full_cone_nat_enabled = true
  sip_alg_enabled       = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `full_cone_nat_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the router uses Full Cone NAT (`nat_enable` in the router API). When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `sip_alg_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the SIP ALG is enabled (`sip_enable` in the router API). When it is not set, the router value does not change.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `network_advanced`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is always "network_advanced".
terraform import glinet_network_advanced.this network_advanced
```
